ting: Heads up — kestrel-liteq int8 canary is showing a weird class of structured-output failures when we exercise multi-step funcalls. Not huge volume but consistent mismatch pattern.

ashley: Any example payload?

ting: Yep, simplest repro we captured:
```
Expected:
{"steps":[{"tool":"search","args":{"q":"LLM inference"}},{"tool":"open","args":{"id":42}}]}

Observed:
{"steps":{"0":{"tool":"search","args":{"q":"LLM inference"}},"1":{"tool":"open","args":{"id":42}}}}
```
The schema validation is strict and treats that as a mismatch (object vs array).

samir: That explains the parse failures we've been seeing in the funcall telemetry. Is it only happening on int8?

eva: Canary dashboard snapshot:
- kestrel-liteq (int8) parse_mismatch_rate: 3.9% over last 6h
- kestrel-fp16 parse_mismatch_rate: 0.08% same period
- affected routes: /v1/chat.invoke (multiturn, tool-heavy prompts)

ting: We also saw similar but much lower in PTQ -> 0.4%. Seems quantization tightness correlates with structural jitter.

ashley: Are the outputs still valid JSON but with numeric keys (stringified ints)? Or are there truncation/escape issues too?
ting: Mostly valid JSON, but numeric-keyed object instead of arrays; occasionally there is extra trailing text after the JSON (suffix noise). Both cause our strict parser to fail.
samir: Two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) parser-rescue that converts numeric-keyed maps back to arrays when the schema expects an array; 2) reject int8 for canary until we patch/retune. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

eva: Can we quantify impact to downstream callers? If we add a rescue heuristic we need to know false positives.

ting: I ran a quick heuristic on a sample of 2k failing outputs: converting numeric-keyed objects to arrays would have salvaged ~72% of failures without touching other valid outputs.

ci-bot: deploy: canary-kestrel-liteq-int8 v2 scheduled to 5% traffic at 2026-03-24T18:00Z by @ting

ashley: OK. Proposed plan:
- Short-term (hotfix): implement conservative parser-rescue that only applies when the expected field is an array, keys are consecutive integer strings starting at 0, and there is no other conflicting type. Ship behind feature flag to 5% traffic.
- Canary monitoring: add metric tag "struct_mismatch_rescued" and capture before/after parse_time and downstream funcall success.
- Medium-term: run quant-sensitivity bench across int4/int8/PTQ/fp16 on the funcall-suite to understand model-side source.

samir: For the medium-term bench, I'll run 10k samples across each quant profile, record parse_mismatch_rate, token-likelyhood, and top-k logits divergence. Command I plan to run:
```
tools/eval_runner --model kestrel-liteq --quant int8 --suite funcall-suite --samples 10000 --record parse_mismatch,logprob,logit_wasserstein --out /tmp/kestrel_int8_funcall.jsonl
```
I'll iterate quant=fp16,int8,ptq,int4.

eva: Also capture kvcache/batch-size config from runtime because batching behaviors can change tokenization boundaries and suffix noise.

ting: Good call. Add runtime tags: batch_size, kvcache_mode, streaming_method.

ashley: If we enable rescue heuristics, we should also produce a repair-warning header in responses so downstreams can opt-in to stricter validation. Something like: X-Structured-Repair: rescued-array(steps)

samir: Agree. That will make telemetry and rollbacks easier.

eva: Scheduling: samir can run bench tomorrow, parser-rescue PR this afternoon (I'll review), then ship feature-flagged rescue to 5% canary. If rescue reduces real parse failures by >50% without increasing silent misrepair rate, we can consider rolling to 25%.

ting: I'll patch canary dashboards to show: parse_mismatch_rate, rescued_rate, downstream_tool_failure_rate, and avg_parse_latency. Can we also capture example pairs (raw+repaired) to a quarantine S3 bucket for manual inspection?

ashley: Yes please — put a 1k sample cap per hour and redact user PII.

ci-bot: metric alert created: eng-ml.parse_mismatch_rate > 2% for 30m -> @eng-ml on-call

samir: One more thought — if numeric-keyed maps are more common for certain prompt templates, let's surface template IDs in telemetry so prompt authors can be notified.

ting: will add prompt_template_id to sample payloads.

eva: Thanks team. If parser-rescue looks safe we get major uptime benefit. If bench shows quantization as root cause we'll re-evaluate quant profiles for production.

ashley: Thanks @samir @ting @eva — I'll coordinate the deploy and reviews. :thumbsup:
